jobs.title: Mum’s walking lantern
jobs.description: “It lights the table. Carry it to the garden and it goes dark. I want to take it to the evening gathering.”

evidence.summary: The light goes out while carried.
Contact: The exposed metal is aged and dull.
Replaced Bulb. Test the object again.
The light goes out while carried.
Cleaned the switch contact faces; run under load and movement to check the result.
The light goes out while carried.
Replaced Switch. Test the object again.

jobs.quote: A family favour. Return it by 17:00 if you can.

jobs.title: The little paper theatre
jobs.description: A cardboard street on a music-box drive. The tune races ahead of the figures. Keep it, improve it, or take your time.

jobs.title: The cracked spare lantern
jobs.description: This object is a donor now. Recover remaining parts; it will not return to service.

jobs.title: Nora’s reading light
jobs.description: “It is bright for a moment, then fades. I read to my nephew after supper. Please test it with the light actually working.”
jobs.quote: £18 if restored and checked. Return by Day 2 · 17:00.

jobs.title: Evan’s small desk fan
jobs.description: “It spins here. Press it against the filter and it slows down. The room gets hot when the windows are closed.”

evidence.summary: Barely a breath of air under load; not enough.

jobs.quote: £32 if restored and checked. Return by Day 2 · 17:00.

jobs.title: Nora’s keepsake music box
jobs.description: “The melody sounds wrong. This was my grandmother’s. A new motor would miss the point; I want this one to work.”

evidence.summary: Replaced Gear. Test the object again.
The melody keeps its pace under load.

jobs.quote: £26 if restored and checked. Return by Day 2 · 17:00.

jobs.title: Sam’s winding toy
jobs.description: “On the bench, the melody stops; while driving the figures, the melody stops. I picked this up with my sister. No hurry if you want to try.” I want the figures to turn at 18 rpm, within one rpm.
jobs.quote: £22 if restored and checked. Return by Day 4 · 17:00.

jobs.title: The meeting-room fan
jobs.description: “At rest, the airflow falls short; through the grille, the airflow falls short. We are opening the room on Saturday. The fan needs to move air through its grille.”
jobs.quote: £24 if restored and checked. Return by Day 4 · 17:00.

jobs.title: The community room fan
jobs.description: The room is ours on Day 4. A fan that moves air through its grille would let Nora read indoors. This is a shared favour, not paid work.

option.label: Work on my own stand and plans

log.speaker: Sam
log.text: I want to learn to handle a whole repair myself. I still have my own plans and promises.

log.speaker: Mum
log.text: I used this lantern on the walk home when you were small. It still has work left in it.

log.speaker: Sam
log.text: I have the morning free. If you want company, I’d like to see how you find the fault. I promised to help my sister later.

log.speaker: Workshop
log.text: Time waits for your decisions. Tests leave evidence. Parts and promises are finite.

log.speaker: Workshop
log.text: Recovered one working switch. The donor is now committed to salvage.

log.speaker: Mum
log.text: Mum’s walking lantern is back in use.

log.speaker: Workshop
log.text: Word of the family repair reaches the neighbours. Three requests are waiting. You do not have to accept all of them.

log.speaker: Sam
log.text: I’m back this morning. I have my own afternoon promise again.

log.speaker: You
log.text: I’ll take responsibility for Nora’s reading light by Day 2 · 17:00.

log.speaker: You
log.text: I’ll take responsibility for Evan’s small desk fan by Day 2 · 17:00.

log.speaker: You
log.text: I’ll take responsibility for Nora’s keepsake music box by Day 2 · 17:00.

log.speaker: Nora
log.text: Nora’s keepsake music box is back in use. Received £26.

log.speaker: Workshop
log.text: £4 covers consumables and shared workshop costs for today.

log.speaker: Evan
log.text: I’ll bring you something new once my small desk fan is back.

log.speaker: Workshop
log.text: Two neighbours have brought work. Their requests can wait while you decide what fits.

log.speaker: Mum
log.text: We can use the room and garden tomorrow. The site opens at noon; people arrive at 15:00. We have time to prepare two formats, at most. Your paper theatre could be one of them.

log.speaker: Sam
log.text: I’m back this morning. I have my own afternoon promise again.

log.speaker: Nora
log.text: You said Day 2 · 17:00 for my reading light. I’m still waiting. If it can’t be done, tell me and give it back.

log.speaker: Evan
log.text: You said Day 2 · 17:00 for my small desk fan. I’m still waiting. If it can’t be done, tell me and give it back.

log.speaker: Evan
log.text: Thank you for telling me what remains. I’ll make another plan. It came back later than promised.
